title: Short communication: Mpox memes, the gift that conceals a blade
screen_reason: Although framed as a qualitative content analysis, the paper reports a quantitative share with an explicit denominator: of 200 mpox memes collected from Google, X, Instagram, Reddit, TikTok and Facebook (Aug-31 Oct 2024), '40% conveyed misinformation or perpetuated stigma'. That is a share of items in a sample classified as misinformation, so it meets the CONTENT criterion - though the numerator is a composite of misinformation AND stigma, which the notes flag.

estimates.country: Not stated; English-language memes, sample 'predominantly reflects English-speaking regions'; authors based in Uganda
estimates.platform: Google, X (formerly Twitter), Instagram, Reddit, TikTok, Facebook
estimates.date: August 2024 (mpox declared a PHEIC) to 31 October 2024
estimates.measure_type: % of sampled mpox memes that conveyed misinformation or perpetuated stigma
estimates.denominator: 200 English-language mpox memes identified via the hashtag #mpox and a Google search for 'mpox memes' (which returned compilations of memes from the six platforms), plus snowballing from comment sections, for posts between August 2024 and 31 October 2024
estimates.definition: Meme coded into the theme 'Misinformation and Stigma': it circulated misinformation (exaggeration/fearmongering about severity or lethality, conspiracy theories about mpox origins) or perpetuated stigmatization of specific groups, particularly the LGBTQ+ community
estimates.misinfo_def: No formal definition given; operationalised through the coded themes - "The memes were coded for themes of awareness promotion, humor, misinformation, and stigma" - with misinformation exemplified by memes that 'suggested the disease was either uncontainable or far more lethal than reported' and memes that 'endorsed conspiracy theories related to mpox origins'
estimates.source_quote: A substantial portion (40%) of the memes circulated misinformation or perpetuated stigma- tization of specific groups, such as the LGBTQ+ community.
estimates.page_loc: p. 3, Results section 3.2 'Misinformation and stigma'; also Abstract and Discussion
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Thematic coding by the two authors; no codebook, coder count per item, double-coding or reliability statistic is reported, and percentages are given as approximations ('Approximately 60%', 'Roughly 20%', 'Around 5%'). Raw metadata for the 200 memes is provided as supplementary S1 Data.
estimates.moderator_quote: Memes were identified using the hashtag #mpox, a google search with the term "mpox memes" returned a compilation of memes shared in the different social media platforms. ... Where retrieved posts had no memes, we used snowballing to collect memes from the comments and comment reply section.
estimates.notes: borderline=true and confidence=low for three reasons an adjudicator must weigh. (1) COMPOSITE NUMERATOR: 'misinformation OR stigma' mixes falsity with prejudice - a factually accurate meme that stigmatises LGBTQ+ people is counted, so 40% overstates misinformation. From the sub-themes, the misinformation-only part is exaggeration/fearmongering (20%) plus conspiracy theories (5%) = 25%, with targeted stigmatisation 15%; that 25% is a cross-category sum, so R8 forbids using it as a value. (2) SAMPLING: memes were harvested from Google 'mpox memes' compilations and snowballed from comment threads - a convenience sample of shareable/viral memes with no defined universe. (3) MEASUREMENT: percentages are approximate, no reliability statistics, single short communication with two authors coding. Value is verbatim so the row is kept, but it should carry heavy uncertainty weight.

missed_or_uncertain: SUB-THEME SHARES NOT EXTRACTED, because their denominator is genuinely ambiguous. Section 3.2 reads 'Roughly 20% of these memes amplified the perceived severity...', 'Another 15% of memes included stigmatizing language...', 'Around 5% of memes endorsed conspiracy theories...'. Read literally, '20% of these memes' means 20% of the 40% misinformation/stigma subgroup; but 20+15+5 = 40 exactly reproduces the theme total, and in the awareness section 25+20+15 = 60 likewise reproduces that theme total, so the authors almost certainly mean percent of ALL 200 memes while writing 'of the awareness-oriented memes'. The purest misinformation estimate in the paper - 'Around 5% of memes endorsed conspiracy theories related to mpox origins' (10/200 if read as all memes; ~4/200 if read as 5% of the 40%) - is therefore left out rather than recorded with a denominator that could be wrong by a factor of 2.5. If an adjudicator resolves the ambiguity from S1 Data, two definition-variant rows become available: conspiracy theories 5% and exaggeration/fearmongering 20% of all memes. Also not extracted: the awareness-theme shares (60% overall; symptom recognition 25%, prevention 20%, trusted voices 15%), which are the complement and not misinformation; and all engagement claims ('These memes often generated high engagement', 'were shared widely'), which carry no numbers.

rob.design: Convenience sample of 200 English-language mpox memes gathered between August and 31 October 2024 via #mpox, a Google search for 'mpox memes' returning cross-platform compilations, and snowballing from comment and reply sections across Google, X, Instagram, Reddit, TikTok and Facebook; no sampling frame, no per-platform counts, no date-stratification beyond checking share dates on Google; qualitative thematic coding by the two authors with no codebook, no double-coding and no reliability statistic; percentages reported as approximations; healthcare-professional status taken from self-reported profile bios with explicitly no secondary validation; authors note the sample reflects English-speaking regions only and that no systematic cross-regional comparison was made.
rob.item6_quote: The memes were coded for themes of awareness promotion, humor, misinformation, and stigma.
rob.item10_quote: A total of 200 mpox-related memes were analyzed, revealing two primary themes: (1) Awareness and Education, and (2) Misinformation and Stigma. ... A substantial portion (40%) of the memes circulated misinformation or perpetuated stigmatization of specific groups, such as the LGBTQ+ community.
